The inventory

Product families in the Census API catalog, split by the Bureau's own dataset flags. The split matters: published uncertainty exists on aggregate tables and does not exist on microdata.
TypeFamiliesWhat that means here
Aggregate tables244Published estimate tables. This is where published uncertainty lives: margins of error, allocation tables, variance replicate tables.
Microdata235Record-level files. Nothing is published per estimate - replicate weights ship with the data and the analyst computes their own standard errors.
Time series93Multi-year series reached through a single endpoint.
Unflagged1The catalog record carries none of the Bureau's aggregate / microdata / time-series flags.

Hand-written headline cards, edited in FINDINGS in product_scope.py. Each also appears on its product card.
1.4% → 13% → 20%Income error explodes as geography shrinksacs/acs5 • nb 01
Median income CV at county / tract / block group; worst cases exceed the incomes measured.
−0.5Sampling noise follows the size law almost exactlyacs/acs5 • nb 02
Fitted slopes −0.47 to −0.51 vs the theoretical −0.50; predictable, therefore scoreable.
80%Tract-level poverty is low-reliability almost everywhereacs/acs5 • nb 01-02
Poverty exceeds CV 0.30 in 80% of NJ tracts and partially defies the size law (slope −0.18).
ρ = −0.58Poverty data is most reliable where poverty is highestacs/acs5 • nb 03
Urban cores measure best, affluent suburbs worst: an equity-relevant blind spot.
~9×Block groups carry ~9× the privacy noise of tractsdec/das-demo • nb 04
Same data, adjacent levels; geography type, not just size, drives DAS noise.
807 / 427Ghost and vanished blocksdec/das-demo • nb 04
807 empty blocks gain 4,695 phantom residents; 427 inhabited blocks publish as empty.
4 in 10Income is imputed for ~39% of households at a typical tractacs/acs5 • nb 05
Age/race under 1%: imputation is a variable-type story, concentrated in income.
ρ ≈ 0Imputation is independent of the published error barsacs/acs5 • nb 05
Every size-controlled allocation-vs-CV correlation sits in [−0.00, +0.19]: the MOE cannot see this error.
22.8%The CV-only blind spotacs/acs5 • nb 06
481 of 2,109 tracts look fine by the error bar but carry heavily imputed income.
84.6%Combining rules disagree at the marginacs/acs5 • nb 06
Equal-weight vs worst-component agree on only ~85% of the top-risk quartile.
R² ≈ 0.67Score the estimate, not the placeacs/acs5 • nb 07
Estimate size alone explains ~2/3 of CV variance; place population almost nothing.
131The quiet tractsacs/acs5 • nb 02
6% of NJ tracts publish population MOEs near zero with no documented reason.

Read straight from WORKLOG.md, newest first. Every sentence is quoted as the teammate wrote it - nothing is summarised, rephrased or scored. Add an entry to the log and it appears here on the next run.
Product scope tracker: PRODUCT_MATCH coverage + --export csv/xlsx2026-07-25 • Garrett Spangler
Evidence coverage jump: 2020 DHC went from 0 → 3 receipts (notebook 04 cell 3, analysis/dhc.py line 36, data-dictionary); Composite prototype 0 → 2 (notebooks 06/07); Allocation analysis 0 → 5 (notebooks 05/06/07, pull_acs_alloc_nj.py, data-dictionary); CV driver model 0 → 1 (notebook 07). All four now register as Validated on the Home tab
New tracked products are our own methodology, not Census products — they surface on the Home tab's "What is in the repo" table but do not attach to any catalog family card, because no family maps to them (FAMILY_TO_PRODUCT untouched). This is deliberate: Composite prototype etc. are our work products, and the Census catalog has no equivalent path
Judgment call, "allocation" as a matcher: the plain word appears in Bureau documentation and product descriptions across the catalog — matching it would over-count. Chose alloc.py, analysis.alloc, from analysis import ... alloc, and pull_acs_alloc instead, which hit only real code references
Export field coverage: Product ID / Name / Family / Status / Repo Evidence / Geography Levels come from real data; MOE Var Count / Allocation Groups are populated only for probed products (currently none — no product_probes.json on the repo yet); Notes falls back to uncertainty_metrics when the free-text note is blank; Agency, Last Reviewed By, Last Reviewed Date are not in the tool's data model and export as empty
The tool auto-creates product_review.json (573 default cataloged entries) on first run — per tool README this file IS committed as team-owned state, but it is not part of these two enhancement commits and can be committed separately at the team's discretion

Repo-state flag: notebooks 06/07 on main import analysis/alloc.py/composite.py/cv_model.py, which exist only on origin/JL_Work_Tree — they cannot run from main until that branch merges; merge + local re-execution + unit tests queued as next-work #1. No changes were made to Justus's work itself

R² ≈ 0.005Place-pop-only R² ≈ 0.005 (JL failure reproduced)

EDA 06: composite reliability prototype (ACS CV × allocation matrix)2026-07-18 • Justus Long • EDA 06
22.8%Blind spot is large for income: among 2,109 classified tracts, 22.8% are low CV (≤ 0.30) but high income allocation (above the exploratory NJ 75th percentile ≈ 0.46) — CV alone would treat these as fine
84.6%Matrix stays the headline: equal-weight vs worst-component agree on only 84.6% of top-risk-quartile membership (162 tracts each exclusive) — combination rules matter at the margin; do not lock weights yet
Matched-size check: within household-count quartiles, income-allocation IQR stays > 0.05 and quadrant mixes still differ — size does not collapse the imputation axis (consistent with EDA 05)
Product boundary held: no row-join of 2010 DHC privacy noise into the ACS score. Poverty uses the labeled family-allocation proxy; Black 65+ uses age/race allocation only as a diagnostic axis. Mentor decisions logged in README
Phase 1 findings report + first Bureau biweekly deck2026-07-17 • Andrew Swiniarski
Decision: presentation/report binaries in /docs ARE committed (lead call, 2026-07-18) — the deck and report ship with the repo; regenerating charts stays a notebook job. EDA 05: allocation rates — imputation prevalence + independence from sampling noise (Phase 1, Step 5 COMPLETE)2026-07-17 • Andrew Swiniarski • EDA 05
~39%Imputation is prevalent and variable-driven: at the median NJ tract ~39% of households had some income imputed (family-poverty proxy ~41%) vs. <1% for age/race and ~0.05% for sex — three orders of magnitude across items; county overall rates 11.5–16.4%
Independence confirmed — the multi-component composite score is empirically justified (Q2): every size-controlled allocation-vs-CV correlation at tract level sits in [−0.00, +0.19]; block group agrees
ρ = −0.18The size control mattered: the poverty pairing's raw ρ = −0.18 collapsed to +0.02 once size was removed — the raw association was pure tract-size confound; future correlation-with-CV analyses should default to the controlled version
Surprise/landmine: B98031/B98032 (the Bureau's ready-made overall allocation rates) are county-only — the API returns tract/BG rows with all-null values (probe lesson: returned rows ≠ returned values)
ρ +0.19Weak income association (controlled ρ +0.19) logged as a mentor question. Decisions: E-only pull; family-universe poverty proxy labeled everywhere; top-coded-income exclusion carried over from EDA 01/02; rate derivation kept notebook-local (graduates to analysis/alloc.py if the composite score adopts it, per the dhc.py precedent)
EDA 04: privacy noise measured — DAS demonstration vs. published 2010 SF1 (Phase 1, Step 5)2026-07-16 • Andrew Swiniarski • EDA 04
The slope hypothesis is directionally confirmed: within-level slopes for total population are −0.78 (block) / −0.85 (block group) / −0.90 (tract) — far steeper than the −0.5 sampling law (EDA 02) and near the −1 constant-absolute-noise ideal, so the two dominant noise mechanisms follow measurably different laws (honest caveat: absolute noise grows several-fold within a level, so exactly −1 it is not)
Surprise — the block-group anomaly: absolute noise by level is non-monotonic; block groups (RMSE 23.2 people) run ~9× tracts (2.5) and ~3.4× blocks (6.9); a same-size block group is ~12× noisier than a tract; for the P12B subgroup table, county is noisiest in absolute terms (34.6). Level — i.e., where the privacy-loss budget is spent — is a first-class reliability factor; mechanism hypothesis (off-spine block groups) logged as a mentor question, not asserted
0.30Practical: total-population privacy noise crosses the 0.30 caution convention only below ~21-person blocks and is negligible (≤0.2%) at tract/county scale; the Black 65+ subgroup sits at ~0.3–0.4 relative noise at the median tract (18 people) — same order as, but ~2–3× smaller than, its ACS sampling CV (0.886, EDA 02)
Ghost/vanished blocks are a categorical artifact class: 807 blocks gain 4,695 phantom residents, 427 lose all 1,154 of theirs
Errors sum to exactly 0 at every level for total population (state invariant propagating down); the subgroup's statewide +16 error propagates identically — hierarchical consistency observed live
2010 SF1 baseline pull + DHC demonstration-file parser (EDA 04 groundwork)2026-07-16 • Andrew Swiniarski • EDA 04
1/21/2,010/6,320/169,588All sanity checks pass on both sides; record counts match 1:1 at every level (1/21/2,010/6,320/169,588). Full-count additivity confirmed on SF1 (every level sums to exactly 8,791,894). SF1 API variable naming gotcha documented: P001001/P012B020 convention (not P0010001), and PCT012B020 exists as a different table. Decision (lead-approved 2026-07-16): EDA 04 scope = total population + Black 65+ parallel, down to block level, binned-relative-RMSE headline metric
DAS demonstration data located + downloaded; data dictionary started (runbook Step 6)2026-07-15 • Andrew Swiniarski
Provisional vintage choice (mentor question updated in README): 2022-08-25 is the newest tabulated demonstration release and nearest to DHC production settings — the 2023-04-03 production suite ships only national microdata (15 GB + 9.4 GB CSVs, impractical) and the 2022-03-16 tabulated release has an April 2022 technical-issues ALERT in its folder, so it was skipped. Gotcha for teammates: the archive's directory-index pages frequently time out (Cloudflare 524) — deep-link to files directly, as the script does. Baseline for the noise comparison (EDA #4) will be published 2010 SF1 tables via the API
EDA 03: tract-level reliability choropleth, dashboard prototype (Phase 1, Step 5)2026-07-15 • Andrew Swiniarski • EDA 03
Not one of NJ's 2,181 tracts reaches the high-reliability tier for poverty (income: 44% do; 92% of tracts are below CV 0.30 for income vs. 21% for poverty)
−0.58poverty-data reliability maps as the inverse of poverty itself — Spearman −0.58 between poverty rate and poverty CV; median CV 0.31 in the poorest quartile of tracts vs. 0.49 in the least-poor quartile. Urban cores (Newark, Camden, Trenton, Atlantic City) are the most reliable places for poverty data; affluent/suburban tracts the least — an equity-relevant blind spot for anyone tracking suburbanizing poverty
Classed tiers + explicit gray class communicate at a glance; carried forward as dashboard design seeds. Phase 1 Step 5's "done when" (notebooks committed, 2–3 mentor-ready charts) is now satisfied
EDA 02: CV by variable type + first derived estimate (Phase 1, Step 5)2026-07-15 • Andrew Swiniarski • EDA 02
The sampling-noise law holds for size-driven counts — fitted log-log slopes: population −0.47, Black 65+ aggregate −0.51, vs. theoretical −0.50
−0.18poverty defies it (slope −0.18) — bigger poverty counts mean poorer tracts, not bigger samples, so its reliability is capped by prevalence (explains EDA 01's "80% of tracts unreliable" shocker)
0.886 → 0.631aggregation helps but doesn't rescue subgroups: median CV 0.886 → 0.631 (1.4×) and coverage 11–50% → 73% of tracts, yet 87% of nonzero tracts stay above CV 0.30
10%the handbook zero-cell rule trims a median 10% (max 55%) off plain-RSS MOEs — adopted as default, documented in glossary
surprise, unexplained: 131 tracts (all 21 counties) publish population MOEs of ±14–143 vs. median ±546 — near-controlled precision with a published MOE; cause unknown, logged as a mentor question rather than guessed at. Composite-score implications: estimate magnitude is a strong free predictor for counts, but variable type must be its own component
EDA 01: CV by geography size (Phase 1, Step 5)2026-07-15 • Andrew Swiniarski • EDA 01
0.014Central empirical fact confirmed: median income CV 0.014 (county) → 0.128 (tract) → 0.204 (block group); worst-case income MOE ±$3,982 → ±$247,531. Surprises worth flagging:
0.30 in 80%tract-level poverty exceeds CV 0.30 in 80% of NJ tracts — a policy-critical variable is low-reliability almost everywhere planners would use it
≈ 0.9Black 65+ single cells are effectively noise at tract level (median CV ≈ 0.9) and are zero in 50–89% of tracts — supports aggregating the six cells in EDA 02
every top-coded income (41 tracts, 270 block groups) ships with no MOE at all, and 2 non-top-coded block groups also lack income MOEs (unexplained annotation — logged for the data dictionary)
county population MOEs are all blank because the estimates are controlled (very reliable) — the "two opposite meanings of a missing MOE" landmine seen live. Decisions per the approved EDA plan: zero estimates → CV undefined; top-coded incomes excluded from CV distributions; thresholds 0.12/0.30/0.40 cited descriptively only (our tiers = later mentor decision)
US boundary pull & exploration2026-07-14 • Katie Christiansen
National analysis is limited to state and county levels for now because nationwide tract and block-group geometry is substantially larger and slower to manage. Estimates include 90% margin-of-error columns
Team sync recap deck; work log started2026-07-12 • Andrew Swiniarski
First mentor meeting set for July 22, 2026 — we bring a one-slide status and the CV-by-geography chart. Open items from the sync: workstream assignments (analysis / dashboard / methodology write-up / data hunting), repo-review feedback, confirming the recurring biweekly slot
NJ boundary pull + 1:1 join verification (Phase 1, Step 5)2026-07-09 • Andrew Swiniarski
Join checks passed 1:1 at every level. 6 invalid geometries at tract level and 6 at block group (self-intersection quirks) — harmless for choropleths, but make_valid must run in the future processing layer before any area/overlay math
ACS 5-year NJ data pull with MOEs (Phase 1, Step 4)2026-07-09 • Andrew Swiniarski
Three data landmines found and documented:
poverty (B17001) and race×age (B01001B) tables are not published below tract level — tract confirmed as the floor, mentor question logged
censusdis converts ACS annotation codes to NaN, collapsing "controlled/very reliable" and "insufficient sample/unreliable" into identical blanks
median income is top-coded at $250,001. Decision: data/raw/ stays exactly as the API returned it; all cleaning belongs in a future processing layer
Repo, environment, and secrets setup (Phase 1, Steps 1–3)2026-07-09 • Andrew Swiniarski

Curated insights (10)
1.4% → 13% → 20%Income error explodes as geography shrinksnb 01
Median income CV at county / tract / block group; worst cases exceed the incomes measured.
−0.5Sampling noise follows the size law almost exactlynb 02
Fitted slopes −0.47 to −0.51 vs the theoretical −0.50; predictable, therefore scoreable.
80%Tract-level poverty is low-reliability almost everywherenb 01-02
Poverty exceeds CV 0.30 in 80% of NJ tracts and partially defies the size law (slope −0.18).
ρ = −0.58Poverty data is most reliable where poverty is highestnb 03
Urban cores measure best, affluent suburbs worst: an equity-relevant blind spot.
4 in 10Income is imputed for ~39% of households at a typical tractnb 05
Age/race under 1%: imputation is a variable-type story, concentrated in income.
ρ ≈ 0Imputation is independent of the published error barsnb 05
Every size-controlled allocation-vs-CV correlation sits in [−0.00, +0.19]: the MOE cannot see this error.
22.8%The CV-only blind spotnb 06
481 of 2,109 tracts look fine by the error bar but carry heavily imputed income.
84.6%Combining rules disagree at the marginnb 06
Equal-weight vs worst-component agree on only ~85% of the top-risk quartile.
R² ≈ 0.67Score the estimate, not the placenb 07
Estimate size alone explains ~2/3 of CV variance; place population almost nothing.
131The quiet tractsnb 02
6% of NJ tracts publish population MOEs near zero with no documented reason.

Aggregate tablesZIP Code Business Patternsvintages 1994–2018 • United States • Bureau documentation
ZIP Code Business Patterns (ZBP) is an annual series that provides economic data by ZIP Code. This table includes the number of establishments, employment during the week of March 12, first quarter payroll, and annual payroll for All Industries by 5-digit ZIP Code. All Industries is set using SIC=00 from 1994 to 1997 and then with NAICS=00 from 1998 to present.
